verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एवं सम्पूजितो राजा पाण्डवैरम्बिकासुतः। विजहार यथापूर्वमृषिभिः पर्युपासितः॥१॥
verses.english: Thus adored by the Pandavas, the royal son of Ambika passed his time happily as before, waited upon and honoured by the Rishis.

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मदेयाग्रहारांश्च प्रददौ स कुरूद्वहः। तच्च कुन्तीसुतो राजा सर्वमेवान्वपद्यत॥२॥
verses.english: That perpetuator of Kuru's race used to make those foremost of offerings which should be given to the Brahmanas. The royal son of Kunti always placed those articles at Dhritarashtra's command.

verses.sanskrit: आनुशंस्यपरो राजा प्रीयमाणो युधिष्ठिरः। उवाच स तदा भ्रातॄनमात्यांश्च महीपतिः॥३॥
verses.english: Shorn of malice as king Yudhishthira was, he was always affectionate towards his uncle. Addressing his brothers and ministers, the king said, 'King Dhritarashtra should be honoured both by myself and you all. He, indeed, is a well-wisher of mine who obeys the commands of Dhritarasthra,

verses.sanskrit: मया चैव भवद्भिश्च मान्य एष नराधिपः। निदेशे धृतराष्ट्रस्य यस्तिष्ठति स मे सुहृत्॥४॥
विपरीतश्च मे शत्रुर्नियम्यश्च भवेन्नरः। पितृवृत्तेषु चाहःसु पुत्राणां श्राद्धकर्मणि॥५॥
verses.english: He, on the other hand, who treats him otherwise, is my enemy. Such a man should certainly be punished by me. On days of performing the rites ordained for the Pitris, as also in the Shraddhas performed for his sons and all well-wishers, the great Kuru king Dhritarashtra, gave away to Brahmanas, as each deserved immense quantity of wealth after his heart.

verses.sanskrit: सुहृदां चैव सर्वेषां यावदस्य चिकीर्षितम्। ततः स राजा कौरव्यो धृतराष्ट्रो महामनाः॥६॥
verses.bhavadeepa: पितृवृत्तेषु पिता वृत्तः प्रमीतो येषु तेषु क्षयाहेषु॥५॥

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणेभ्यो यथार्हेभ्यो ददौ वित्तान्यनेकशः। धर्मराजश्च भीमश्च सव्यसाची यमावपि॥७॥
तत्सर्वमन्ववर्तन्त तस्य प्रियचिकीर्षया। कथं नु राजा वृद्धः स पुत्रपौत्रवधार्दितः॥८॥
verses.english: King Yudhishthira the just, and Bhima, and Arjuna, and the twins, desirous of doing what was liked by the old king, used to execute all his cominands.

verses.sanskrit: शोकमस्मत्कृतं प्राप्य न म्रियेतेति चिन्त्यते। यावद्धि कुरुवीरस्य जीवत्पुत्रस्य वै सुखम्॥९॥
verses.english: They always took care that the old king who was afflicted with the destruction of his sons and grandsons, with, that is, grief caused by the Pandavas themselves, might not die of his grief.

verses.sanskrit: बभूव तदवाप्नोति भोगांश्चेति व्यवस्थिताः। ततस्ते सहिताः पञ्च भ्रातरः पाण्डुनन्दनाः॥१०॥
verses.english: Indeed, the Pandavas treated him in such a way that that Kuru hero might not be deprived of that happiness and all those articles of enjoyment which he had during his sons lifetime.

verses.sanskrit: तथाशीलाः समातस्थुर्धृतराष्ट्रस्य शासने। धृतराष्ट्रश्च तान्सर्वान्विनीतान्नियमे स्थित्तान्॥११॥
verses.english: The five brothers, viz., the sons of Pandu, treated thus Dhritarashtra, living under his command.

verses.sanskrit: शिष्यवृत्तिं समापन्नान्गुरुवत्प्रत्यपद्यत। गान्धारी चैव पुत्राणां विविधैः श्राद्धकर्मभिः॥१२॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra also, seeing them so humble and obedient to his commands and acting towards him as disciples towards preceptors, treated them also like a loving preceptor in return.

verses.sanskrit: आनृण्यमगमत्कामान्विप्रेभ्यः प्रतिपाद्य सा। एवं धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥१३॥
verses.english: Gandhari, by performing the various rites of the Sharaddha and making gifts to Brahmanas of various objects of enjoyment, became freed from the debt she owed to her slain children.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रातृभिः सहितो धीमान् पूजयामास तं नृपम्।
              वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              स राजा सुमहातेजा वृद्धः कुरुकुलोद्वहः॥१४॥
verses.english: Thus did that foremost of righteous men, viz., king Yudhishthira the just, endued with great intelligence, along with his brothers, adored king Dhritarashtra.

verses.sanskrit: न ददर्श तदा किञ्चिदप्रियं पाण्डुनन्दने। वर्तमानेषु सद्वृत्तिं पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु॥१५॥
verses.english: Vishampayana said Endued with great energy, that perpetuator of Kuru's race, viz., the old king Dhritarashtra, could not see any ill-will in Yudhishthira.

verses.sanskrit: प्रीतिमानभवद्राजा धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः। सौबलेयी च गान्धारी पुत्रशोकमपास्य तम्॥१६॥
verses.english: Seeing that the great Pandavas were in the observance of a wise and righteous conduct, king Dhritarashtra, the son of Ambika, became pleased with them.

verses.sanskrit: सदैव प्रीतिमत्यासीत्तनयेषु निजेष्विव। प्रियाण्येव तु कौरव्यो नाप्रियाणि कुरूद्वहः॥१७॥
verses.english: Subala's daughter, Gandhari, renouncing all sorrow for her (slain) children, began to show great love for the Pandavas as if they were her own children.

verses.sanskrit: वैचित्रवीर्ये नृपतौ समाचरत वीर्यवान्। यद्यद्ब्रूते च किञ्चित्स धृतराष्ट्रो जनाधिपः॥१८॥
verses.english: Gifted with great energy, the Kuru king Yudhishthira never did anything that was disliked by the royal son of Vichitravirya. On the other hand, he always treated him in a highly agreeable way.

verses.sanskrit: गुरु वा लघु वा कार्यं गान्धारी च तपस्विनी। तं स राजा महाराज पाण्डवानां धुरन्धरः॥१९॥
verses.english: Whatever acts, grave or light, were directed by king Dhritarashtra or the helpless Gandhari to be done, were all done with respect, O monarch, by that destroyer of hostile heroes, viz., the Pandava king.

verses.sanskrit: पूजयित्वा वचस्तत्तदकार्षीत्परवीरहा। तेन तस्याभवत्प्रीतो वृत्तेन स नराधिपः॥२०॥
अन्वतप्यत संस्मृत्य पुत्रं तं मन्दचेतसम्। सदा च प्रातरुत्थाय कृतजप्यः शुचिर्नृपः॥२१॥
verses.english: The old king became highly pleased with such conduct of Yudhishthira. Indeed, he was grieved at the remembrance of his own wicked son.

verses.sanskrit: आशास्ते पाण्डुपुत्राणां समरेष्वपराजयम्। ब्राह्मणान्स्वस्ति वाच्याथ हुत्वा चैव हुताशनम्॥२२॥
verses.english: Rising every day at early dawn, he purified himself and went through his recitations, and then blessed the Pandavas by wishing them victory in battle.

verses.sanskrit: आयूंषि पाण्डुपुत्राणामाशंसत नराधिपः। न तां प्रीतिं परामाप पुत्रेभ्यः स कुरूद्वहः॥२३॥
verses.english: Indeed, the king had never derived that great happiness from his own sons which he always did from the sons of Pandu.

verses.sanskrit: यां प्रीतिं पाण्डुपुत्रेभ्यः सदावाप नराधिपः। ब्राह्मणानां यथावृत्तः क्षत्रियाणां यथाविधः॥२४॥
तथा विट्शूद्रसङ्घानामभवत्स प्रियस्तदा। यच्च किञ्चित्तदा पापं धृतराष्ट्रसुतैः कृतम्॥२५॥
verses.english: King Yudhishthria at that time became as agreeable to the Brahmanas the Kshatriyas, and the various bands of Vaishyas and Shudras of his kingdom.

verses.sanskrit: अकृत्वा हृदि तत्पापं तं नृपं सोऽन्ववर्तत। यश्च कश्चिन्नरः किञ्चिदप्रियं वाम्बिकासुते॥२६॥
verses.english: as to King Yudhishthira forgot whatever wrongs were done to him by the sons of Dhritarashtra, and saluted his uncle.

verses.sanskrit: कुरुते द्वेष्यतामेति स कौन्तेयस्य धीमतः। न राज्ञो धृतराष्ट्रस्य न च दुर्योधनस्य वै॥२७॥
verses.english: If any man did nay thing that was not liked by the son of Ambika, he became thereby an object of hatred to the intelligent son of Kunti. Indeed, through fear of Yudhishthira nobody could talk of the evil deeds of either Duryodhana or Dhritarashtra.

verses.sanskrit: उवाच दुष्कृतं कश्चिद्युधिष्ठिरभयानरः। धृत्या तुष्टो नरेन्द्रः स गान्धारी विदुरस्तथा॥२८॥
verses.english: Both Gandhari and Vidura also were well pleased with the power which the king having no enemics showed for bearing wrongs. They were, however, not so pleased, O destroyer of foes, with Bhima.

verses.sanskrit: शौचेन चाजातशत्रोर्न तु भीमस्य शत्रुहन्। अन्ववर्तत भीमोऽपि निश्चितो धर्मजं नृपम्॥२९॥
धृतराष्ट्रं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य सदा भवति दुर्मनाः। राजानमनुवर्तन्तं धर्मपुत्रममित्रहा। अन्ववर्तत कौरव्यो हृदयेन पराङ्मुखः॥३०॥
verses.english: That destroyer of enemies, secing Dharma's son pay his respects to the old king, saluted him outwardly with a very reluctant heart.
